symptoms: Water-soaked irregular greenish-black foliage lesions; white downy sporulation underneath under high humidity; firm greasy brown fruit rot.
spread_mechanism: Windblown sporangia and splashing rain; favored by temperatures 15-22°C and relative humidity >90%.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil MZ) @ 1.5 - 2.0 kg/ha in 500-750 L water (or 2.5 - 3.0 g/L). Organic alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha; Copper Hydroxide 77% WP.
bio_alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha; Copper Hydroxide 77% WP
safety_notes: Observe strict 7-day pre-harvest interval (PHI). Spray early morning or late afternoon. Wear protective eye and skin gear. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with concentric 'target board' rings on older leaves, progressing upward.
spread_mechanism: Survives in crop debris and soil; spread by rain splash, wind, and equipment in warm weather (24-29°C).
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5 - 2.0 kg/ha or Azoxystrobin @ 500 ml/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha; Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC).
recommended_dosage: 1.5 - 2.0 kg/ha or Azoxystrobin @ 500 ml/ha in 500 L water
bio_alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha; Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC)
safety_notes: 5-day PHI. Rotate fungicide modes of action (FRAC codes) to prevent Alternaria resistance. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 5 days.

symptoms: Small (2-3 mm) water-soaked circular dark brown spots with chlorotic yellow halos; blister-like scabs on fruit.
spread_mechanism: Seed-borne and rain splash in warm humid conditions (25-30°C).
cibrc_approved_pesticides: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP + Streptomycin sulphate 9% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 1% SP (Streptocycline 100-200 ppm)
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP + Streptomycin sulphate 9% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 1% SP (Streptocycline 100-200 ppm) @ Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 - 0.2 g/L. Organic alternative: Bacillus subtilis 1% WP seed treatment and foliar spray; Copper soap.
bio_alternative: Bacillus subtilis 1% WP seed treatment and foliar spray; Copper soap
safety_notes: Streptocycline must only be applied during active vegetative stage as prescribed by DPPQ&S. 7-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface; velvety olive-brown spore layer on lower surface.
spread_mechanism: Airborne conidia thriving in stagnant greenhouse air with humidity >85%.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 kg/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Trichoderma harzianum foliar spray; improve greenhouse canopy ventilation.
bio_alternative: Trichoderma harzianum foliar spray; improve greenhouse canopy ventilation
safety_notes: Ensure greenhouse vent circulation to keep humidity below 85%. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with greyish-white centers and dark brown margins studded with tiny black pycnidia.
spread_mechanism: Splashing rain and dew; persistent in solanaceous weeds and old crop litter.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 1.5 - 2.0 kg/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP foliar spray.
bio_alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP foliar spray
safety_notes: Spray at first sign on lower leaves; destroy crop residue after harvest. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Yellow stippling and speckling on foliage; fine silken webbing under leaves; bronzing and defoliation.
spread_mechanism: Hot, dry, dusty weather; mites disperse by crawling and wind currents.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Propargite 57% EC (Omite) @ Spiromesifen @ 500 ml/ha or Propargite @ 1.5 L/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Azadirachtin 1% (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L; predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
recommended_dosage: Spiromesifen @ 500 ml/ha or Propargite @ 1.5 L/ha in 500 L water
bio_alternative: Azadirachtin 1% (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L; predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis)
safety_notes: Ensure thorough coverage of leaf undersides where mites colonize. 3-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 3 days.

symptoms: Pinpoint brown spots expanding into zonate target lesions with chlorotic halos; pitted lesions on fruit.
spread_mechanism: Airborne spores under warm (20-28°C), humid tropical conditions.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (Amistar Top) @ 1.0 ml/L for Amistar Top or 2.5 g/L for Mancozeb. Organic alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha.
recommended_dosage: 1.0 ml/L for Amistar Top or 2.5 g/L for Mancozeb
bio_alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha
safety_notes: Avoid overhead irrigation; 5-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 5 days.

causal_microbe: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus / Geminiviridae)
symptoms: Severe plant stunting; upward curling of leaf margins; severe chlorosis and mottling; flower drop.
spread_mechanism: Transmitted persistent-circulative by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci); not seed-borne.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Vector Control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (Confidor) @ Imidacloprid @ 150 ml/ha or Thiamethoxam @ 200 g/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Yellow sticky traps (20-25/ha); Neem oil 1500 ppm; barrier netting (50 mesh).
recommended_dosage: Imidacloprid @ 150 ml/ha or Thiamethoxam @ 200 g/ha in 500 L water
bio_alternative: Yellow sticky traps (20-25/ha); Neem oil 1500 ppm; barrier netting (50 mesh)
safety_notes: Viral infections cannot be cured with chemical sprays; manage whitefly vectors immediately and rogue infected plants. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 5 days.

symptoms: Mottling and alternating light/dark green mosaic on leaves; fern-leaf distortion; internal browning of fruit.
spread_mechanism: Easily spread by direct mechanical contact, worker hands, contaminated pruning tools, and infected seed.
cibrc_approved_pesticides: Skimmed milk spray (10%) during seedling handling
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Seed Treatment: Trisodium Orthophosphate (TSP 10%) soak @ 10% TSP solution for 30 min seed soak, followed by thorough rinse. Organic alternative: Strict field sanitation; rogue and burn infected plants; wash hands with soap/skimmed milk.
recommended_dosage: 10% TSP solution for 30 min seed soak, followed by thorough rinse
bio_alternative: Strict field sanitation; rogue and burn infected plants; wash hands with soap/skimmed milk
safety_notes: Chemical pesticides are ineffective against virions. Prevent mechanical transmission by hands and pruning shears. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Uniform vibrant green foliage without spots, curling, chlorosis, or necrotic tissue.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Maintain preventive neem sprays and balanced organic vermicompost.
bio_alternative: Maintain preventive neem sprays and balanced organic vermicompost
safety_notes: Harvest freely. Safe for direct human consumption. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown-black foliar blotches with white downy growth underneath in morning dew; dry tuber rot.
spread_mechanism: Cull piles, infected seed tubers, and windborne sporangia travelling miles in humid cloudy weather.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0 kg/ha for Mancozeb or 1.5 kg/ha for Metalaxyl+Mancozeb. Organic alternative: Trichoderma harzianum seed tuber treatment @ 10 g/kg; Copper Hydroxide.
recommended_dosage: 2.0 kg/ha for Mancozeb or 1.5 kg/ha for Metalaxyl+Mancozeb
bio_alternative: Trichoderma harzianum seed tuber treatment @ 10 g/kg; Copper Hydroxide
safety_notes: Mandatory 7-day PHI. Destroy potato vine haulms 14 days before harvest to avoid tuber contamination. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Small brown angular spots with target concentric rings; leaves yellow and dry up.
spread_mechanism: Overwinters in crop debris; splashing rain and wind in alternating wet/dry weather.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5 - 2.0 kg/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha foliar spray.
bio_alternative: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha foliar spray
safety_notes: 7-day PHI. Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Broad, vibrant green foliage without spots or leaf-margin browning.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Continue regular earthing-up and balanced potassium nutrition.
bio_alternative: Continue regular earthing-up and balanced potassium nutrition
safety_notes: Harvest when tubers mature. Tubers are completely safe for food use. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Olive-green velvety spots turning into corky dark scabs on leaves and developing fruit.
spread_mechanism: Ascospores discharged from overwintered leaves during spring rain at 16-24°C.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Difenoconazole @ 30 ml/100 L water or Mancozeb @ 250 g/100 L water. Organic alternative: Wettable Sulfur 80% WP @ 300 g/100 L water; orchard floor urea 5% spray in autumn.
recommended_dosage: Difenoconazole @ 30 ml/100 L water or Mancozeb @ 250 g/100 L water
bio_alternative: Wettable Sulfur 80% WP @ 300 g/100 L water; orchard floor urea 5% spray in autumn
safety_notes: 14-day PHI. Start preventive sprays at green tip through petal fall. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots with purple margins; firm brown rot with alternating light/dark rings turning fruit into mummies.
spread_mechanism: Overwinters in bark cankers and mummified fruit; conidia splash during rainfall.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ Copper Oxychloride @ 300 g/100 L water or Captan @ 200 g/100 L water. Organic alternative: Prune out dead wood and cankers; apply Bordeaux paste to pruning cuts.
recommended_dosage: Copper Oxychloride @ 300 g/100 L water or Captan @ 200 g/100 L water
bio_alternative: Prune out dead wood and cankers; apply Bordeaux paste to pruning cuts
safety_notes: Prune during winter dormancy. Observe 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface; cup-shaped fungal aecia structures on underside.
spread_mechanism: Heteroecious fungus cycling between apple and Juniperus virginiana via windborne basidiospores.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Nativo @ 40 g/100 L water or Mancozeb @ 250 g/100 L water. Organic alternative: Remove alternate host red cedar/juniper trees within 500m of orchard.
recommended_dosage: Nativo @ 40 g/100 L water or Mancozeb @ 250 g/100 L water
bio_alternative: Remove alternate host red cedar/juniper trees within 500m of orchard
safety_notes: Apply from pink bud to petal fall. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Lush, deep green leaves with crisp margins and glossy cuticle.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Maintain regular orchard floor sanitation and balanced nutrition.
bio_alternative: Maintain regular orchard floor sanitation and balanced nutrition
safety_notes: Safe for consumption and export. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular leaf spots; berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
spread_mechanism: Ascospores and pycnidiospores ejected during warm rainy periods (21-27°C).
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Mancozeb @ 2.0 kg/ha or Myclobutanil @ 400 g/ha in 600 L water. Organic alternative: Bordeaux Mixture 1% (10:10:100); canopy opening to sunlight.
recommended_dosage: Mancozeb @ 2.0 kg/ha or Myclobutanil @ 400 g/ha in 600 L water
bio_alternative: Bordeaux Mixture 1% (10:10:100); canopy opening to sunlight
safety_notes: Spray from early shoot growth through 4 weeks post-bloom. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic/necrotic foliar striping; dark purple spotting on berries; wood vascular necrosis.
spread_mechanism: Spore infection through pruning wounds; slow internal vascular spread.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ Wound paint: Bordeaux paste 10% on pruning wounds. Organic alternative: Trichoderma atroviride wound protectant; remove infected cordons.
recommended_dosage: Wound paint: Bordeaux paste 10% on pruning wounds
bio_alternative: Trichoderma atroviride wound protectant; remove infected cordons
safety_notes: Sterilize pruning tools between vines. Discard severely diseased wood. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Large, irregular dark brown lesions with defined red-brown borders on mature leaves.
spread_mechanism: Favored by late-season humid rains and dense grapevine canopies.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Mancozeb @ 2.0 kg/ha in 500-600 L water. Organic alternative: Bordeaux Mixture 1%; post-harvest pruning clearance.
bio_alternative: Bordeaux Mixture 1%; post-harvest pruning clearance
safety_notes: Spray immediately after post-monsoon pruning. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Vibrant emerald-green palmately lobed leaves with no discolored patches.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Maintain proper shoot thinning and trellising for optimal air movement.
bio_alternative: Maintain proper shoot thinning and trellising for optimal air movement
safety_notes: Ready for harvest and fresh table or wine consumption. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

pathogen_type: Bacterium (Vector: Asian Citrus Psyllid Diaphorina citri)
symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle chlorosis on leaves; yellow shoots; small, lopsided, sour green fruit with aborted seeds.
spread_mechanism: Transmitted by Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) and infected grafting budwood.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Vector Control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ Imidacloprid @ 0.5 ml/L water or Thiamethoxam @ 0.3 g/L water. Organic alternative: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%); release Tamarixia radiata parasitoids.
recommended_dosage: Imidacloprid @ 0.5 ml/L water or Thiamethoxam @ 0.3 g/L water
bio_alternative: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%); release Tamarixia radiata parasitoids
safety_notes: Control psyllid vectors at bud burst. Remove unproductive trees (rogueing). 15-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 15 days.

symptoms: Angular, water-soaked purple-black spots on leaves, falling out to give 'shot-hole' look; cracked fruit pits.
spread_mechanism: Windblown rain and dew; overwinters in twig cankers and buds.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L or Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L. Organic alternative: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens foliar spray; dormant copper spray at leaf fall.
recommended_dosage: Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L or Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L
bio_alternative: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens foliar spray; dormant copper spray at leaf fall
safety_notes: Avoid phytotoxic high copper doses on young peach foliage after shuck split. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Smooth lanceolate leaves with vibrant green coloration and no necrotic holes.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Maintain regular orchard floor mulching and pruning.
bio_alternative: Maintain regular orchard floor mulching and pruning
safety_notes: Completely safe for harvest and consumption. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Small irregular chlorotic spots on leaves becoming necrotic and brown; raised scab-like spots on peppers.
spread_mechanism: Overwinters on infected seed and solanaceous weeds; dispersed by driving rain.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP + Streptocycline 100 ppm @ Copper Hydroxide @ 2.0 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L. Organic alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed.
bio_alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment @ 10 g/kg seed
safety_notes: 7-day PHI. Do not work in fields when bell pepper foliage is wet. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

symptoms: Glossy, uniform deep green leaves without blistering or necrotic spots.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Ensure regular calcium nutrition to prevent blossom end rot.
bio_alternative: Ensure regular calcium nutrition to prevent blossom end rot
safety_notes: Safe for consumption. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: Rectangular, brown to gray lesions strictly bounded by leaf veins; blighting of canopy.
spread_mechanism: Windblown spores from infected maize crop residue in warm, humid, overcast weather.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole @ 1.0 ml/L or Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L. Organic alternative: Trichoderma viride seed treatment @ 4 g/kg seed.
recommended_dosage: Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole @ 1.0 ml/L or Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L
bio_alternative: Trichoderma viride seed treatment @ 4 g/kg seed
safety_notes: Apply when threshold shows lesions on the ear leaf at tasseling. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Oval to elongated reddish-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, erupting with powdery spores.
spread_mechanism: Windblown urediniospores travelling long distances; favored by 16-25°C and high humidity.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Propiconazole @ 1.0 ml/L water or Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L water. Organic alternative: Plant rust-resistant hybrid varieties; Trichoderma foliar spray.
recommended_dosage: Propiconazole @ 1.0 ml/L water or Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L water
bio_alternative: Plant rust-resistant hybrid varieties; Trichoderma foliar spray
safety_notes: 14-day PHI. Spray when pustules appear before flowering. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Large, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long).
spread_mechanism: Overwinters in corn residue; conidia blown by wind and rain during cool wet weather (18-27°C).
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Mancozeb 75% WP @ Mancozeb @ 2.0 kg/ha in 500 L water. Organic alternative: Deep ploughing of maize stubble; Trichoderma viride seed treatment.
bio_alternative: Deep ploughing of maize stubble; Trichoderma viride seed treatment
safety_notes: Apply at early whorl stage if disease is observed. 14-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 14 days.

symptoms: Long, arched, vigorous dark green leaves with clean parallel venation.
spread_mechanism: N/A
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: No chemical spray @ N/A - No pesticide application required. Organic alternative: Balanced nitrogen and zinc application.
bio_alternative: Balanced nitrogen and zinc application
safety_notes: Safe for fodder and food consumption. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 0 days.

symptoms: White talcum-powder-like fungal patches expanding across leaf surfaces and stems; leaves turn yellow and crisp.
spread_mechanism: Windblown conidia; thrives in dense shaded canopies with warm dry weather and high relative humidity at night.
treatment_options: Apply CIB&RC approved formulation: Wettable Sulfur 80% WP @ Wettable Sulfur @ 2.5 - 3.0 g/L or Hexaconazole @ 1.0 ml/L water. Organic alternative: Potassium Bicarbonate @ 3 g/L; Ampelomyces quisqualis biopesticide; Neem oil 1500 ppm.
recommended_dosage: Wettable Sulfur @ 2.5 - 3.0 g/L or Hexaconazole @ 1.0 ml/L water
bio_alternative: Potassium Bicarbonate @ 3 g/L; Ampelomyces quisqualis biopesticide; Neem oil 1500 ppm
safety_notes: Do not spray sulfur when temperatures exceed 32°C to prevent phytotoxic leaf scorch. 5-day PHI. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 5 days.

bio_alternative: Remove diseased foliage during renovation; Trichoderma viride foliar spray
safety_notes: 7-day PHI. Ensure drip irrigation to keep strawberry foliage dry. Mandatory waiting period (PHI) before harvest: 7 days.

recommended_dosage: Wettable Sulfur @ 2.5 g/L or Myclobutanil @ 0.5 g/L water
